expectations.prediction: SPLIT INTO TWO CLAIMS ON PURPOSE, because the harvester's M6 `critic` counter and the question 'did the critic run' are NOT the same thing, and conflating them would let a 0 be reported as 'unchanged from pilot-01'. (A) THE CRITIC RAN: at least one turn's archived pending.json carries `critic.status: "ran"` with `verdicts >= 1`. This is the claim pilot-02 exists to establish. In pilot-01 it was false BY CONSTRUCTION (phases.critic was null), so a Delta here is a real measurement rather than an artifact; it is directly observable and robust at n=12. EXPECTED: true. (B) THE CRITIC SUPPRESSED SOMETHING: M6 `critic > 0`, i.e. at least one finding carries `critic_verdict: "likely_fp"` (harvest.ts:214 counts DEMOTIONS, not invocations — a critic that runs and returns `keep` for everything scores 0). EXPECTED: > 0, on the strength of bench alpha12-v2 attempt-09 (86/86 eligible, -16.7pp clean-case FP rate). REGISTERED IN ADVANCE: a 0 on (B) with (A) true is a REAL and reportable result — the critic looked at this run's findings and kept them — and it is categorically different from pilot-01's 0, which measured nothing. It must not be written up as 'no change'. The critic is also legitimately absent on any turn whose panel produced ZERO findings (orchestrator.ts:2302 runs it only when findings > 0); such turns are excluded from (A)'s denominator, not scored as failures.

At least 3 of the seeds that LAND are caught in their own turn. Carried over from pilot-01's floor, but the denominator is now the LANDED seeds (all five carry a landedPattern), so it is no longer inflated by defects the agent declined to write. pilot-01 measured 0.60 (3/5) as registered and 0.67 (2/3) on landed seeds; neither is citable as an effect size at n=3-5, and neither is this one. The critic is DEMOTE-ONLY and exempts CRITICAL+security/correctness, corroborated and protected-reviewer findings (aggregator.ts:604-618), so recall is expected to be UNCHANGED — a recall DROP against pilot-01 would be the most important negative result this run can produce and must be reported as such, not smoothed over.

The five landedPatterns were calibrated against pilot-01's recorded working-tree.diff and reproduce that hand-verified ground truth exactly (turns 2/7/11 land, 4/9 do not), and each was mutation-checked in both directions against plausible safe and unsafe lines. known_limitations: THE EXPERIMENTAL DELTA, stated exactly: the sandbox config is pilot-01's verbatim plus ONE added block — `phases.critic: { provider: "openrouter", model: "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", persona: "fp-filter" }`. The panel, the provider blocks, loop.runTimeoutMs and every other phase are byte-identical to pilot-01. The rig preregistration schema has no field for a critic (roster.reviewers is strict), which is why it is recorded here.

THE CRITIC MODEL IS PINNED RATHER THAN INHERITED, and that is a deviation from the C1 snippet in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-fp-ledger-evidence-unit-design.md. In THIS repo the snippet resolves to deepseek-v4-flash; in the pilot sandbox providers.openrouter.model is deepseek-v3.2, which is ALSO panel reviewer #1, so an inherited critic would judge its own findings. The pin keeps the critic independent of every panel member and makes it the exact model the cited +4.1pp precision / -16.7pp clean-FP figures were measured with.

NO OPENROUTER UPSTREAM PIN, unlike this repo's own config (`openrouterProvider: { only: ["alibaba"] }`). phases.critic inherits routing from providers.openrouter, so pinning the critic's upstream would re-route the PANEL as well — a second change, which would make pilot-02 non-comparable to pilot-01 on M3. Both the panel and the critic therefore run on OpenRouter's load-balanced upstream, as pilot-01's panel already did. Consequence: the serving upstream (and its quantisation) is not controlled and may differ between iterations. Recorded rather than fixed. Separately: this repo's config comment calling alibaba the cheapest NON-fp8 upstream is stale — the endpoints API reports Alibaba as fp8 for both deepseek models today, so that pin buys upstream determinism, not precision.

`reviewgate doctor` WARNS in this sandbox that the worst-case panel wall clock (630s) exceeds loop.runTimeoutMs (600s), i.e. the critic could be budget-skipped. runTimeoutMs is nonetheless kept identical to pilot-01, because the warning is worst-case arithmetic (every provider burning its full 300s timeoutMs) and the measured reality is not close: across pilot-01's 19 gate runs the SLOWEST used 54.9s, 9.2% of the deadline, leaving 545s against a 45s critic floor (MIN_CRITIC_BUDGET_MS 15s + CRITIC_TAIL_RESERVE_MS 30s). If any turn nevertheless reports `critic.status: "skipped-budget"`, that turn is excluded from the M6 (A) denominator and the exclusion is reported.
n = 12 turns, 5 seeded. A single turn moves recall by 0.20. This detects SIGNAL; it does not establish effect size. Every rate is reported with its raw numerator/denominator and a Wilson 95% CI.

ONE run, and a SECOND run of a different configuration — so any pilot-01 vs pilot-02 difference is confounded with ordinary run-to-run variance in the agent, the panel and the load-balanced upstream. The only comparison this design supports is the one on the critic's own directly-observable activity (M6 (A)), which was zero by construction before and is measured now.

codex is excluded VIA CONFIG (`providers.codex.enabled: false`), not via its quota state — its cooldown ends 2026-08-08T11:07Z and would otherwise have added a reviewer, making the panel a different system from pilot-01's and measuring two changes at once.
The agent is `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits`, whose model and behaviour are outside this repo's control and are NOT pinned by this preregistration. pilot-01 ran under the same constraint.

The ablation is an AGGREGATION-LAYER counterfactual over fixed reviewer output, not a behavioural A/B: it cannot re-drive the agent, because different verdicts would have produced different diffs. Iterations, cost and FP burden are not recomputed under ablation.
fp-ledger's ablation delta would be an INTERVAL, not a point, had it fired: the layer overwrites severity with INFO and the pre-suppression severity is persisted nowhere.

A landedPattern is a positive regex over ADDED lines. It cannot see a guard the agent added on a DIFFERENT line: for path-traversal and check-then-write, a safe implementation that keeps the same call shape but validates elsewhere would still score as landed. The patterns exclude the sanitiser spellings that appear on the same line (basename/normaliz/resolve/sanitiz/valid) and were mutation-checked against safe variants, but this residual is real and the recorded diff.patch is the fallback evidence, exactly as in pilot-01.
Anything that fails, times out or is skipped will be reported per-turn in the result's warnings[], including in the write-up.
